tasks.title: Registry-driven argv classification — migrate the four ssh verbs to templates and delete the hand-maintained if-chain

acceptance.mutation_control: EXECUTED RED 2026-07-28, five controls. (A) length equality -> prefix match: an argv with EXTRA arguments classifies. (B) literal equality -> case-insensitive: 'Systemctl restart nginx' classifies. (C) drop the empty-slot check: 'systemctl restart ""' classifies with an empty value. (D2) `slots != 1` -> `slots > 1`: a zero-slot template classifies, and a COMPILED class (empty template) matches an EMPTY argv — an empty template becomes a wildcard. (E2) ambiguity `return` -> `break`: two classes building the same argv resolve to the first. TWO OF THESE DID NOT FIRE ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT, and both times the ORACLE was at fault, not the mutation. (D) the original clause `len(ArgvTemplate)==0` is REDUNDANT with the length check, so no mutation of it is observable — the real guard is `slots != 1`, and the test was rewritten to drive an empty argv against every compiled class. (E) the live registry is injective, so the double-match branch is UNREACHABLE from any registry-driven test; a `classifyAgainst(specs, argv)` seam was added so an ambiguous pair can be constructed. A branch no test can reach is a branch no control can falsify.
acceptance.notes: The four ssh verbs (restart-service, reload-service, start-service, restart-container) moved from compiled Go builders to argv templates carried as registry data; their compiled builders are DELETED. The equivalence test written in T-013-25 compared the template against the live builder — which became a TAUTOLOGY the moment the verbs migrated, since Lookup then returns the template and it compared the template to itself. It is replaced by hardcoded goldens transcribed from the deleted builders, because an oracle whose subject becomes its own reference has stopped being an oracle. The schema-builder lockstep test now asserts builder XOR template.

tasks.title: A new verb is registry DATA: derived resolvable set, family-keyed vocabulary, declared rollback

acceptance.mutation_control: EXECUTED RED 2026-07-28, six controls, each verified to apply. (A) drop container-lifecycle from the derived set -> 'start-container is a registered ssh-argv class in a known family but does NOT resolve at the leaf'. (B2) WithMutation back to a literal map -> same. (C) rollback becomes a re-run of the forward -> "a start's compensating action must be 'stop', never another start". (D) RollbackTemplate ignored entirely -> same. (E3) the unknown-family default falls through to the unit vocabulary -> 'refused with: target unit is not a valid systemd unit token, want ErrNoExecutionPath'. THREE OF THESE NEEDED THE ORACLE FIXED, NOT THE MUTATION, and each failure was the SAME shape one level up from the bug being fixed: (B) the first test built the Module by STRUCT LITERAL with reversible already seeded, so it proved reversibleFromRegistry() was correct while proving nothing about whether the wired constructor calls it — rebuilt through the real New()+WithMutation. (E) the resolvable-set gate masks the family switch, so the durable state is SEEDED past the first guard, the same technique the tier floor needed. (E2) even seeded, a probe class in an unknown family fails a param lookup either way, so the oracle now asserts the SPECIFIC error: ErrNoExecutionPath ('this leaf does not do that') vs anything else ('the leaf tried and failed incidentally').
acceptance.notes: COST MEASUREMENT, which is the point of the task. Adding start-container as a new verb after this change: ONE JSON block in opschema.json (15 lines), ONE line in the fault injector's Provokes(), and a named constant used only so tests can refer to it. No compiled builder, no case in resolveOp, no entry in a reversible map. Before the T1 work the measured cost was ~120 lines across 8 files per verb.

tasks.title: Cisco interactive-SSH transport (TG-85 slice 1): a read-only PTY send/expect leaf whose command-admission guard structurally refuses everything but a show/diagnostic read — no pipe-to-write, no mode change; ships dark/unwired at never-auto

acceptance.go_test: modules/actuation/cisco: TestExecRefusesEverythingButReadOnly (the read-only admission guard — pipe-to-redirect/tee/append + every mutating verb refused before the runner) / TestExecAdmitsReadOnlyAndRunsIt / TestModuleActuatorContract (ReadOnly unconditional) / TestRunShowEndToEndAgainstFakeCisco (pty+shell+pager-off+show over an in-process fake device) / TestRunShowFailsClosedWithoutKnownHosts / TestRunShowRefusesUnknownHostKey / TestRunShowCtxDeadlineAborts
acceptance.notes: TG-85 write slice 2 (2026-08-22) refactored interactive.go WITHOUT changing the read behavior: the connect / host-key / watchdog / PTY / pager-off setup was extracted into a private dialSession() helper so the separately-gated WRITE lane (configsession.go's config-mode transport) shares exactly ONE verified transport path with RunShow. RunShow is behavior-identical — the TestRunShow* end-to-end + fail-closed tests above prove it — so this task stays completed and read-only; the write lane is a distinct gated type (writer.go), never a flag flip on this one (ADR-0012). TG-85 component 3 (2026-08-23) adds the READ-ONLY SHOW CATALOG beside this task's verb guard, and with it a CREDENTIAL FLOOR on cisco.go's Exec. The slice-1 guard admits any first-token `show` carrying no mutating word — but `show` is a family, and running-config/startup-config carry IPsec pre-shared keys, SNMP communities and password hashes, while `show crypto ikev1 pre-shared-key` prints them outright. Reading a secret is not a mutation, so the mutating-verb guard never refused them. The floor is SCOPE-AWARE: an unscoped config dump and the secret sections (crypto, tunnel-group, aaa-server, snmp-server, all) are refused, while `show running-config interface <if>` stays admitted exactly as TestExecAdmitsReadOnlyAndRunsIt pins it. A Catalog (WithCatalog, optional) further NARROWS admission to a named diagnostic set; with none wired the module is byte-identical to this task's behaviour. The agent-facing read TOOL is deliberately NOT here: registering a tool renders into the model preamble, an eval-visible surface. TG-85 component 2 (2026-08-23) adds JUMP-HOST reachability to interactive.go: a Device may declare a bastion (Device.Jump), and dialSession then dials the bastion, verifies ITS host key against ITS own known_hosts, opens a direct-tcpip channel onward, and runs the DEVICE handshake over that tunnel — so the device key is still verified end-to-end and a compromised bastion can drop the session but never impersonate the device. Written by hand rather than `ssh -J` (no shell, INV-02). A PARTIALLY declared hop refuses the connection and never falls back to a direct dial. The zero value is a direct dial, so this task's existing behaviour is unchanged for a device with no hop. TG-85 component 4 (2026-08-23) adds the REVERSIBLE-OP REGISTRY: a NAMED change carrying its own declared undo, executed by name (WriteModule.ExecOp) rather than as text. It is NARROWER than the prefix path, not wider — the free-form guard is untouched, and a leading `no` becomes expressible only as the declared inverse of a registered op. Four registration rules, each mutation-verified: no op without an undo; the inverse may not equal the forward (the 'start rolls back to start' trap); an op_class on core/safety's non-configurable never-auto floor (interface-shutdown, no-interface, acl-delete, route-delete, erase-startup-config...) cannot register AT ALL, the same clamp the kubernetes leaf applies to delete/drain; and the platform is part of the op identity so an IOS registry never yields ASA's verb (`no shutdown` vs `no shut`), which would leave a change applied and un-revertable. The op SET is empty by default — which changes are safe on this estate is operator policy (config-not-code), not a judgement this package ships.
